prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right one depends on your priorities (budget, timeline, level of prep/detail, paint brands, warranty, etc.). I can help you find the best fit. To narrow it down, tell me your ZIP code/neighborhood and a few preferences (approx. number of rooms or sqft, target budget, desired start date, whether you want specialty finishes).

Meanwhile, use this quick plan to identify the best local painter:

1. Decide priorities
 - Price vs. quality: do you want lowest bid or longest-lasting, detailed work?
 - Scope: single room, whole house, trim/doors, textured/specialty finishes?
 - Timeline and availability
 - Brand of paint (Benjamin Moore, Sherwin-Williams, etc.) or eco-friendly options

2. Where to search
 - Google & Yelp (look for recent 4+ star reviews)
 - Angi/HomeAdvisor, Houzz
 - Better Business Bureau for complaint history
 - Local Facebook community groups / Nextdoor for neighborhood referrals

3. Key qualifications to require
 - Proof of insurance (liability and workers’ comp)
 - Business license and local references
 - Portfolio of recent interior jobs (photos)
 - Written estimate that lists prep, primer, number of coats, paint brand, cleanup, and warranty

4. Questions to ask each painter (use as a checklist)
 - Are you licensed and insured? Can you provide certificates?
 - Do you have local references I can contact?
 - What’s included in the estimate (prep, repairs, primer, # coats, door/window trim)?
 - What paint brand/line will you use and is that included?
 - How do you protect floors/furniture and handle cleanup?
 - Who will supervise the crew? What is your estimated start and completion date?
 - What warranty or touch-up policy do you offer? What are payment terms?

5. How to compare bids
 - Don’t pick by price alone — compare scope, materials, and guarantees.
 - Ask for a written contract and a clear change-order policy.
 - Check 2–3 estimates for the same defined scope.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and a brief description of the job (number of rooms, ceilings/trims, any repairs) and I’ll suggest several well-reviewed St. Louis painters and draft email/text you can send them to request estimates. Which would you prefer?
